# CPP DCMA-14: the one definition

Version 1, 7 November 2026. Every CPP engine that reports a DCMA-14 result measures it exactly as written here:

- the validator (`critical-path-validator/scripts/dcma14.py`; the `critical_path_validator` MCP tool, the claude.ai skill and the public cpp-critical-path-validator copy),
- the health dashboard (`schedule-health-review/template/Schedule_Health_Dashboard_v7_Obsidian.html`; the website demo, the analyst-delivered assessment and the `dcma14_health_check` MCP tool),
- CPP Lens DCMA Lite (`cpp-lens-viewer/src/sections/dcma-lite.js`; the free browser screen).

The constants are in `dcma_definition.json` beside this file. The parity fixtures in `_cpp_common/tests/fixtures/dcma_parity/` carry expected results worked out from this text, and each engine's suite checks itself against them. A change to this definition is made here first, then in all three engines in the same release.

The source is the DCMA EVMS Program Analysis Pamphlet, DCMA-EA PAM 200.1 (October 2012), section 4. Where the pamphlet leaves a choice open, the choice CPP makes is marked **CPP reading**. The thresholds are DCMA's; the A to F grade is CPP's own convention.

## Common rules

**D0 One project.** A file with several PROJECT rows is scored on one: the only row; else the latest `last_recalc_date` as filed (before D14 fills or lifts it), ties broken by the most TASK rows, then file order. Its activities, the relationships with both ends in them, the resource assignments on them and its own data date are used; nothing else in the file is read, except that #1 counts a link to another project (D4). The result names the project scored when the file holds more than one. A file with one PROJECT row is read whole, whatever project ID its activities carry. The project is chosen first and its data date (D14) is then read; every entry point (a direct call, a report, a tool) uses this one choice.

**D1 Activity types.** Ordinary activities: `TT_Task`, `TT_Rsrc` (and any type not listed here). Milestones: `TT_Mile`, `TT_FinMile`, and any ordinary activity whose original duration (`target_drtn_hr_cnt`) is zero: it carries no work, and the pamphlet's populations leave zero-duration tasks out as milestones (a blank duration is not zero). Where a rule names a milestone type (D10's exemptions, D11's tie order), it means that type. Level of effort and WBS summary (`TT_LOE`, `TT_WBS`) are never counted, and a relationship with either end on one is never counted.

**D2 Status.** Complete means `status_code = TK_Complete`; everything else is incomplete.

**D3 Working days.** Hours divided by the hours per day of the activity's own calendar. The hours per day are the calendar's `day_hr_cnt`, except as P6 schedules (measured on P6's own recalculation): when every working day of the week works the same shift hours and `day_hr_cnt` says otherwise, the shift hours; and a calendar record with no shift data is P6's internal 8-hour Standard, whatever it declares. A blank activity calendar is the project calendar (`PROJECT.clndr_id`), else the default calendar (`default_flag = Y`), else 8 hours, and the fallback is disclosed. An activity whose project ID names no project in the file has no project calendar and takes the default; a calendar the activity names but the file does not hold is 8 hours, disclosed.

**D4 Relationships.** *Logic relationships*: both ends in the scored project, neither end LOE or WBS. *Live relationships*: logic relationships whose successor is incomplete (**CPP reading**: a relationship between finished activities is history and is not graded). *Links to another project*: a relationship with one end in the scored project and the other outside it (not a level of effort or WBS summary where the file holds that end), or P6's external early start or external late finish on an activity. P6 schedules them, so for #1 they count as a predecessor or successor and the number of activities linked only that way is disclosed; #2 to #4 judge the scored project's own relationships and do not grade them.

**D5 Dates.**
- Validity (#9) and lateness (#11) are compared by **calendar day**.
- An activity is *due* (#11, #14) when its baseline finish is at or before the data date **to the minute**: a baseline finish later on the data date itself is not yet due (data date 08:00, baseline finish 16:00).
- *Complete as of the data date* (#14): complete, and its actual finish (if any) on or before the data date's day.
- (**CPP reading**: a recorded date is compared by day because P6 stores actual and update dates at a clock time the scheduler rarely chooses; *due* is decided to the minute because a baseline finish later on the data date's own day is work the plan had not yet asked for. So an activity finished at 16:00 on the data date counts as complete while its 16:00 baseline finish is not yet due, one way the index can exceed 1.0.)

**D6 Not scored.** A check whose population is empty, or whose inputs are missing (no data date, no baseline, no computed float, no resource assignments, unreadable forecasts), is NOT SCORED. It stays out of the score's numerator and denominator, and the result gives the reason. Nothing is ever a PASS for want of something to measure.

**D7 Exact counts.** A percentage threshold is tested on the counts (count x 100 against threshold x total), never on a rounded percentage. An index (#13, #14) is compared after rounding to six decimal places, so a CPLI of exactly 0.95 passes: CPLI is a ratio of measured working time, which binary arithmetic cannot always hold exactly, and six places is far finer than any schedule is measured to.

**D8 Activity ID matching** (baseline to current). `task_code` with surrounding spaces trimmed, case ignored. An ID that appears more than once in either the scored project or the baseline project is ambiguous (every activity row counts, level of effort and WBS summary included): activities carrying it are left out of #8's baseline basis and of both counts of #11 and #14, and the number left out is disclosed. No alias matching (A1234 to 1234) and no matching by name. #13 reads the baseline finish of the completion activity's own Activity ID; where that ID appears more than once in the baseline, the first such activity in the file is read. A blank Activity ID matches nothing (P6 requires one; a file without them is malformed).

**D9 Baseline project.** When the baseline file holds several projects: the one with the same `proj_id`, else the same `proj_short_name`, else the one sharing the most Activity IDs with the scored project (ties broken as D0 breaks them). Whatever rule chose it, and however many projects the baseline file holds, a baseline project that shares no Activity ID with the scored project (an ordinary activity or milestone in both; a level of effort or WBS summary row does not count) is not used: #11, #13 and #14 are NOT SCORED, #8 reads current durations, and the result says why.

**D10 Network start and finish** (#1). The network starts at the earliest start (actual, else early, else planned) of any ordinary or milestone activity, complete included. It finishes at the latest finish (actual, else early, else planned) of the incomplete ones. Both are compared to the minute.

**D11 Completion activity** (#12, #13). The ordinary or milestone activity, complete or not, with the latest early finish (read per activity: its early finish, else its planned finish). On a tie: a finish milestone, then an activity of zero original duration (a completion typed as a task), else the first in the file. (**CPP reading**: #1's finish exemption, D10, covers only a `TT_FinMile`, so a completion typed as a zero-duration task is the completion here and can still be an open end in #1; retyping it as a finish milestone is the fix the result points to.)

**D12 Baseline finish** (#11, #13, #14). A baseline activity's finish is its planned finish (`target_end_date`), else its early finish. On an unprogressed baseline the two are the same. (**CPP reading**: a progressed update used as a baseline carries P6's planned dates moved onto actuals as work started; it is read as filed, and the result is only as good as the baseline supplied.)

**D13 Working time** (#13). Measured on the calendar's own shift times: the part of a day before the data date's clock time is not counted, nor the part after a finish's clock time. A data date at the start of a working day and a finish at the end of a working day five working days later is 5.0 working days.

**D14 Data date.** The scored project's `last_recalc_date`. Blank, it is the project's planned start (`plan_start_date`); on a day before a later planned start, it is lifted to the planned start. Both are what P6 does when it opens the project, and the result discloses either.

## The fourteen checks

| # | Check | Population | Counts as a finding | Passes when | Not scored when |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Logic | incomplete ordinary activities and incomplete milestones | no logic relationship in (missing predecessor) or out (missing successor). A `TT_Mile` with no predecessor starting at or before the network start (D10), and a `TT_FinMile` with no successor finishing at or after the network finish, are not findings; the exemption covers only the missing side named (**CPP reading**: a dangling mid-network milestone is the defect #1 exists to find) | activities with either finding (each counted once) are at most 5% | population empty |
| 2 | Leads | live relationships | lag below 0 | none | no live relationships |
| 3 | Lags | live relationships | lag above 0 | at most 5% (a lag over 44 working days on the successor's calendar is listed for information; it decides nothing) | no live relationships |
| 4 | Relationship types | live relationships | Finish-to-Start; any Start-to-Finish is named for information (the pamphlet says it should not be used) | at least 90% are FS | no live relationships |
| 5 | Hard constraints | incomplete ordinary activities | `CS_MSO`, `CS_MEO`, `CS_MSOB`, `CS_MEOB`, `CS_MANDSTART` or `CS_MANDFIN` as the primary or the secondary constraint (DCMA's Must Start On, Must Finish On, Start No Later Than, Finish No Later Than; P6's mandatory pair is harder than any of them). Constrained milestones are listed for information (**CPP reading**: the pamphlet counts tasks, and #1 counts milestones only because a milestone's open end breaks the network) | at most 5% | population empty |
| 6 | High float | incomplete ordinary activities with a computed total float | total float above 44 working days | at most 5% | no incomplete ordinary activity carries a computed float (a blank float is left out and counted) |
| 7 | Negative float | as #6 | total float below 0 | none | as #6 |
| 8 | High duration | incomplete ordinary activities with a readable original duration (a blank or non-numeric one is left out and the count disclosed) | duration above 44 working days. The duration is the baseline's original duration of the same activity (on the baseline activity's calendar) when a baseline is supplied and the activity is in it, else (or when the baseline's is blank) the current original duration (`target_drtn_hr_cnt`); the result says how many were read on each basis. The pamphlet's detail-planning-window restriction is not applied | at most 5% | population empty |
| 9 | Invalid dates | ordinary activities and milestones, complete included | an actual start or actual finish on a day after the data date's day; or, on incomplete work, a forecast before it: not started, an early start or early finish on a day before the data date's day; started, an early finish on a day before it | none | no data date. When the incomplete work carries no early dates the forecasts cannot be read: the actual dates are still judged, and the result says so |
| 10 | Resources | incomplete ordinary activities with an original duration of at least 1 working day (a blank duration is left out) | no resource assignment carrying hours or cost (`target_qty`, `target_cost`, `remain_qty` or `remain_cost` above 0) | every one is resourced (100%) | the scored project carries no resource assignments at all (**CPP reading**: a file with none was exported without them, or is not resource-loaded by design, and 0% would say nothing about the schedule); population empty |
| 11 | Missed tasks | baseline ordinary activities due by the data date (D5), matched to the current schedule (D8) | not in the current schedule (deleted or renumbered); not complete (its forecast finish is necessarily after its baseline finish, which is at or before the data date, so this is the pamphlet's finish comparison); or complete with an actual finish on a day after its baseline finish. Complete with no actual finish: lateness unknown, out of both counts (**CPP readings**: deleted work counts as missed, because work the baseline committed to is not done; the 80% floor stops a renumbered schedule being read as wholesale misses; #14 counts such an activity as complete because #14 asks only whether it is done, not when) | at most 5% | no baseline; no data date; nothing due; fewer than 80% of the due activities match the current schedule |
| 12 | Critical path test | the network | FAIL, with no recalculation needed, on a logic cycle or on an incomplete completion activity (D11) pinned by `CS_MANDSTART` or `CS_MANDFIN` as its primary or secondary constraint (a complete completion activity's pin decides nothing: there is no remaining network for a delay to move, and P6 does not apply a constraint to finished work). Otherwise the test is run where a CPM recalculation is available (CPP's validator, and the health report it renders): the schedule is recalculated as filed and again with 600 working days added to the remaining duration of the *test activity* (and to its expected finish where P6 honours one): the incomplete ordinary activity on the completion activity's driving path nearest the data date whose finish drives the next activity on that path (Finish-to-Start or Finish-to-Finish; a duration delay does not pass along a Start-to-Start link), the completion itself excluded. An unfinished activity nearer the data date that drives the path only through its start (Start-to-Start) cannot carry a duration delay, so once that test passes the nearest such activity takes a start delay instead: its start is held 600 working days after its as-filed early start (a Start On or After in a free constraint slot), and that result decides #12. Where a Mandatory Start in its primary slot already holds its start (its start sits on that date, or the constraint drives it), the start cannot take the delay and the test FAILS there (P6 offers no mandatory constraint in the second slot; an imported file that carries one is scheduled by P6, and by the recalculation, as a floor like Start On or After (P6 probes of 19 October 2026), so it does not hold a start. The completion's pin above is read in either slot because that FAIL is decided without a recalculation: **CPP reading**, the conservative one); any other start constraint does not hold a start against a later date, so the delay is inserted and judged by the move. Where it has started or carries two constraints, the stretch is named as not tested; where its start does not take the delay for no reason the test can name, the test is NOT SCORED. Where every unfinished activity on the path drives it through its start, the start delay on the nearest one is the test. If its finish does not move by the delay because an expected finish or its resources set it, the next one along is tried, up to three. If a finish constraint holds it (a duration delay moves a finish, so only a finish constraint can: its recalculated finish, as filed or delayed, sits on the constraint's date, a date on a non-working day counting as the working time beside it; or the engine names a constraint as its driver, as where a Mandatory Finish later than its logic leaves a gap that absorbs part of the delay), the test FAILS there and says how far the completion moved. If its finish does not take the delay for no reason the test can name, the test is NOT SCORED and says so. PASS when the completion's early finish moves by the delay (working time on the test activity's calendar, less up to one working day for rounding). Where the full move came along another path (an activity on the as-filed driving path did not move), it passes and names that activity and any constraint it sits on. A smaller move later passes only when the logic demonstrably carried the delay and the calendars can account for the rest: the engine still names the test activity back from the completion, every activity after it on the as-filed driving path moved later, none on that path or on the delayed driving chain had its finish set by an expected finish or sits on a constraint's date, and the path crosses another calendar or carries a lag or lead; the result then says which set the amount (**CPP reading**: the calendar rule). FAIL otherwise, naming where the delay is lost: the first activity after the test activity on the as-filed driving path that moved by less than the delay and did not move, sits on its constraint's date, had its finish set by an expected finish or is now driven by something other than the path's previous activity (failing those, the first that moved by less), and what holds it: that constraint, the expected finish (with how far its start moved), or its new driver and that driver's constraint or expected finish. The recalculation is CPP's CPM engine, not P6: where its as-filed completion differs from the file's by more than a working day, and where P6's own longest-path flag in the file marks activities on the tested path as off its longest path, the result says so. A Mandatory Start dated before the data date, and a Mandatory Finish the work cannot meet from the data date, do not hold the work: P6 starts it at the data date (P6 probes of 13 October 2026), and so does the recalculation. The test delays one driving path: another unfinished predecessor of the completion at the driving predecessor's total float, which the delay did not reach, is named as not tested. NOT SCORED where no unfinished ordinary activity drives the completion, where the path is carried only by Start-to-Start links and no start delay can be inserted, where no delay could be inserted, where the network is larger than the test can be run on (5,000 activities), or where the recalculation does not finish in time (20 seconds for the run as filed, 60 for the whole test; a network over 100 activities is recalculated in a separate process that is stopped at the limit); where only a constraint drives the completion, FAIL. (**CPP reading**: the pamphlet does not fix the delay, the activity or a tolerance; 600 working days and the activity nearest the data date are common practice, and the one-day tolerance, the three tries and the calendar rule are CPP's.) A view that cannot recalculate (the in-browser dashboard, CPP Lens) decides only the certain FAIL cases and reports the rest as not scored. Network screens (orphans, an unreachable finish, a split critical network) are reported for information | the completion moves by the delay | no unfinished ordinary activity drives the completion; the completion activity is complete; it has no predecessor (#1's finding); no recalculation available |
| 13 | CPLI | the completion activity (D11) | (critical path length + float) / critical path length. Critical path length: the working time (D13) from the data date to its early finish on the project calendar, in working days. Float: with a baseline, the working time from that early finish to the baseline finish (D12) of the same activity, measured the same way (else the baseline's own completion activity, disclosed); without one: where the file names a deadline date (the project's Must Finish By, or the date of a `CS_MEO` or `CS_MEOB` on the completion; the earliest when several), the working time (D13) from the completion's early finish to that date on the project calendar, negative when the finish is later, so both terms are in the project calendar's working days; with no named date, its P6 total float on its own calendar where that float is not zero (P6 measured it against some date), disclosed | at least 0.95 | no data date; the completion activity is complete (no remaining critical path); an unfinished completion activity pinned by `CS_MANDSTART` or `CS_MANDFIN` (P6 sets its finish and float from the constraint, so CPLI would read 1.000 by construction; #12 fails it instead); a baseline supplied but not used (D9); no baseline and no deadline, and a zero float (1.000 by construction) or none exported; finish at or before the data date |
| 14 | BEI | baseline ordinary activities due by the data date, including those no longer in the current schedule | the current ordinary activities complete as of the data date (D5), every one counted (ambiguous IDs aside, D8), so the index can exceed 1.0 (**CPP reading**: the pamphlet's extra denominator term for tasks with no baseline finish is not added) | at least 0.95 | no baseline; no data date; nothing due |

CPP Lens scores checks 1 to 11 (11 needs a baseline). #12 needs a CPM recalculation and #13 the critical path length, neither of which Lens computes, and Lens leaves #14 to the full assessment, so it reports all three as not scored, except that #12 is a FAIL there too on a logic cycle or a mandatory-constrained completion.

## Results and the grade

- Every result is PASS, FAIL or NOT SCORED, with the counts behind it (numerator and denominator). There is no intermediate band.
- The validator reports passed / scored. The dashboard also gives a letter: pass rate = passed / scored, rounded to the whole percent shown; A at 90 and above, B 75, C 60, D 45, else F; band GREEN at 85 and above, YELLOW 65, else RED. It is CPP's convention, not DCMA's, it is printed with "n of 14 scored", and no letter or band is given when fewer than 10 of the 14 could be scored.
- The validator's nuclear and mining profiles change some thresholds; a result graded on one names the profile and says the threshold is CPP's, derived from the DCMA check. The published numbers above are the default (commercial) profile.
